\footnotesize\textit{Note}: \texttt{elementwise\_binary} covers \texttt{add},
\texttt{sub}, \texttt{mul}, \texttt{div} (T-BROADCAST rule);
\texttt{reduce} covers \texttt{sum}, \texttt{mean}, \texttt{max}, \texttt{min}
(T-REDUCE rule).  The structural reshape \texttt{flatten} reduces to
\texttt{view} on a deterministic shape function
(\texttt{squeeze}/\texttt{unsqueeze}/\texttt{dropout} have been
promoted to Lean-audited this round). The activation family
\texttt{relu}/\texttt{gelu}/\texttt{silu}/\texttt{tanh}/\texttt{sigmoid}
plus \texttt{softmax}/\texttt{detach} are
shape-preserving by Lemma~EU on the elementwise lift.
\texttt{pad} has a deterministic linear shape function and
\texttt{where} reduces to broadcast (a 3-ary \texttt{T-Broadcast}
instance).  All thirteen carry a self-contained proof sketch in
the reproducibility appendix and are checked by the same
$1{,}000$-sample property test as the Lean rules.
The non-trivial case is \texttt{einsum}, whose explicit pen-and-paper
soundness statement is given immediately below
(\Cref{prop:einsum-soundness}); the remaining $12$ pen-and-paper
rules have shape functions that are either elementwise lifts
(activation family, \texttt{detach}), strict
shape-preservation (\texttt{flatten}), reductions over a fixed axis-set
(\texttt{reduce}), or instances of broadcast
(\texttt{elementwise\_binary}, \texttt{where}).
\end{minipage}

\begin{proposition}[Soundness of the \texttt{einsum} pen-and-paper rule]
\label{prop:einsum-soundness}
Let an \texttt{einsum} call have left-hand-side subscripts
$L=(L^{(1)},\dots,L^{(n)})$ where $L^{(i)}\in\Sigma^{*}$ for an
alphabet $\Sigma$ of axis labels, with input tensors of
symbolic shapes $\bar d^{(1)},\dots,\bar d^{(n)}$ such that
$|L^{(i)}|=|\bar d^{(i)}|$ for each $i$ (subscript-arity
condition). Let $R\in\Sigma^{*}$ be the right-hand-side
subscript with no repeated label (output-uniqueness
condition) and $R\subseteq\bigcup_i L^{(i)}$ (output-coverage
condition). Define the per-label envelope
$\mathrm{env}(\ell):=\{\bar d^{(i)}_j : L^{(i)}_j=\ell\}$ for
each $\ell\in\Sigma$. The rule's precondition is the
\emph{label-consistency obligation}
$\bigwedge_{\ell\in\Sigma}\bigwedge_{d,d'\in\mathrm{env}(\ell)}
(d=d')\vee(d=1)\vee(d'=1)$ (broadcast-axis identification),
and the rule's output shape is
$\bar d^{R}_k:=\max\,\mathrm{env}(R_k)$ for each $k$ (the
broadcast resolution; well-defined on satisfying assignments).
\textbf{Soundness.} If the precondition is discharged by Z3
on $\Gamma\models\varphi_{\mathrm{op}}$ and the subscript-arity,
output-uniqueness, and output-coverage syntactic conditions
hold, then for every $\sigma\models\Gamma$ the runtime
\texttt{torch.einsum} call with the same subscripts on
$\sigma(\bar x)$ either succeeds with output of shape
$\bar d^{R}$ (under the rule's symbolic image
$\sigma(\bar d^R)$) or raises a runtime exception on the
violated label-consistency check, by direct case analysis on
the \texttt{at::native::einsum} dispatch.
\textbf{Refutation completeness.}
If Z3 produces a model $\mathfrak{m}$ falsifying the
label-consistency obligation, the heap
$\sigma_{\mathfrak{m}}$ of \Cref{def:model-extraction} drives
the runtime call into the same exception branch, discharging
\Cref{thm:soundness}(ii) on this handler.
\end{proposition}
